scenes.title: UC Davis & Max Planck Brain Imaging Suite: 1985 Billboard Headphones Lighting Up the Spared Midline Musical Sanctuary
scenes.era: 2009–2015, UC Davis Center for Mind and Brain & Max Planck 7-Tesla Neuroimaging Suite

layout.description: Bright glass-walled neuroimaging control room pairing classic 1980s vinyl record sleeves and studio headphones beside a dual-screen 7-Tesla brain monitor showing the glowing midline frontal-cingulate musical island standing bright inside an otherwise dimmed Alzheimer's scan.

positions.who: Petr Janata (neuroscientist in dark blazer and open-collar blue shirt)
positions.where: standing at the audio-fMRI console sliding the studio fader up to play a 30-second 1985 Billboard excerpt while pointing to the glowing medial prefrontal trace
positions.facing: angled between the mixing fader and the brain-scan display

positions.where: seated upright in the sunlit observation chair, lifting chin and tapping fingers on armrest in instant word-for-word song recognition

props.name: cushioned over-ear studio headphones and 1985 vinyl record sleeve stack
props.period_detail: tactile youth-era Billboard music physical anchors wired to precision lab audio deck
props.physical_behavior: State-A listener sits quiet with hands still in lap -> State-B researcher pushes audio fader forward and listener lifts head, taps fingers in rhythm, and sings effortlessly

props.name: 7-Tesla brain comparison monitor ('Spared Midline Musical Island vs Faded Hippocampus')
props.period_detail: high-contrast clinical neuroimaging display pairing Janata 2009 MPFC tracking with Jacobsen 2015 spared hub
props.physical_behavior: State-A dim baseline cortical map -> State-B midline ventromedial prefrontal and cingulate island lights bright cyan in sync with the chord change

actions.verb_sequence: places cushioned headphones over the listener's ears and slides the console fader up on a random 30-second youth track
blinks at the first three guitar chords -> sits up straight, taps right hand briskly on the chair arm, and sings every lyric without hesitation

reactions.reaction: beams with vivid emotional warmth transported forty years back in three seconds
traces the glowing midline prefrontal-cingulate hub confirming the 42.3% autobiographical lock

scenes.wardrobe: Smart academic navy blazer and Oxford shirt; warm oatmeal knit cardigan on older listener.
scenes.lighting: Warm natural tall-window daylight balanced with crisp cyan neuroimaging screen glow.
scenes.recognition_hook: Forget a new name in five seconds, yet put on a 1985 song and a sheltered midline island in your brain sings every word.

key_visual.description: a sunlit neuroimaging studio where a researcher slides up an audio fader beside 1980s vinyl sleeves as an older adult in cushioned headphones sits up singing and a 7T monitor highlights the spared midline frontal-cingulate hub

scenes.title: Outdoor Backyard Patio Handshake to Sunlit Car Dashboard Radio: Dropping 'Greg' vs Nailing Every 1985 Lyric
scenes.era: Modern sunlit Saturday afternoon backyard patio and tree-lined suburban street

layout.description: Open-air sunlit backyard patio table leading out to a parked car along a leafy neighborhood curb.

positions.where: shaking a new neighbor's hand on the sunny patio, pausing blankly five seconds later by the gate, then climbing into the car, pressing the dashboard radio knob, and belting out a 1985 chorus
positions.facing: from sunlit outdoor patio to open-window car driver's seat

props.name: paper barbecue name tag and classic rotary car-radio volume knob
props.period_detail: everyday adult neighborhood social cue contrasted with tactile car dashboard dial
props.physical_behavior: State-A driver shakes hands and glances blankly at empty palm five seconds later -> State-B twists car radio knob clockwise and taps steering wheel singing every word

actions.verb_sequence: shakes hands on the patio and stalls trying to recall the name -> climbs into the sunlit car, clicks the radio knob on, and taps the wheel singing every lyric

reactions.reaction: laughs out loud at the contrast between a 5-second name blank and 40-year-old lyric perfection

scenes.wardrobe: Casual weekend linen shirt and sunglasses pushed up on forehead.
scenes.lighting: Bright golden late-afternoon outdoor sunlight through street trees.
scenes.recognition_hook: A new name hangs by one fragile hippocampal thread—a 1985 song is braided across four brain hubs at once.

scenes.title: Outdoor Sunlit Courtyard Bench: Adult Daughter Sharing a '1965–1975 Youth Playlist' With Her Aging Father

layout.description: Peaceful sunlit garden bench under a pergola where an adult daughter places lightweight headphones on her 78-year-old father.

positions.where: sitting side by side on the outdoor wooden garden bench as she presses play on a saved youth-era song list
positions.facing: turned warmly toward each other in morning sunlight

props.name: silver retro headphone band and pocket music player
props.period_detail: personalized favorite-music care intervention modeled on King et al. (2019) and Cuddy et al. (2015)
props.physical_behavior: State-A father sits slumped looking down quietly -> State-B daughter slips headphones on and presses play, and father lifts head smiling and conducting the beat

actions.verb_sequence: gently places the headphones over her father's ears and presses play on his twenty-song youth playlist
lifts his chin within two seconds, smiles wide in recognition, and conducts the melody with one hand

reactions.reaction: share immediate eye contact and connection as the spared musical hub wakes up whole-brain synchrony

scenes.wardrobe: Soft sky-blue sweater on daughter; plaid flannel shirt and cardigan on father.
scenes.lighting: Warm dappled outdoor morning garden sunlight.
scenes.recognition_hook: Twenty songs from ages 12 to 25 form a lifelong neural bridge even Alzheimer's struggles to touch.
